texts: The first lighting of a new lantern is a small ritual.
Each Council member touches the vessel of mire-essence before the first lighting.
A replacement lantern needs no Council touch.

fields.sentence: The first lighting of a new lantern is a small ritual.

q1_issues.issue: The Ordinal atom ranks the lantern instead of the lighting - 'the first lighting' makes the lighting the first, so putting the lantern witness in Ordinal's entity slot asserts that the lantern is first on a lighting ordering.

'the lighting of a new lantern' is a nominalization whose of-phrase is its object, which Complements of nouns and adjectives routes to the entity-attached surface-preposition oblique on the noun's own symbol rather than to a Patient role on a reified verb event, and the deverbal noun 'lighting' is derivation, so taking the verb lemma 'light' as the class crosses the inflection-only line of Names and casing.

The sentence is a characterizing/customary generic, but the parse mints specific witnesses for the lighting and the lantern and predicates ritual-hood of them, against the generic-claim instruction that a nominalized-clause subject never mints a witness for itself in the generic reading.

q2_gaps: generic copular predication whose subject is a nominalized event ('The first lighting of X is a small ritual') - the gerund/nominalized-subject rule routes only a verbal main predicate into a per-occurrence Skolem consequent and gives no form for a kind/property ascribed to the occurrence itself

an ordinal restriction on a nominalized-event subject ('the FIRST lighting') has no stated carrier inside the generic/rule route - Ordinal is defined over entities ranked on a scale, not over a rule's occurrence variable
review.notes: The predicate split 'small ritual' into two atoms rather than fusing, which is right (size adjective = incidental description). All heads used are licensed; the defects are role/slot choices and the specific-versus-generic level of the whole parse.

issues.reason: `Ordinal <entity> <n> <scale>` ranks the entity in its first slot, so `(Ordinal sk_lantern_1 1 light)` asserts the lantern is first on a lighting ordering — a falsehood, since the text ranks the lighting, not the lantern.

"A nominalization's of-phrase is its OBJECT, not a genitive" routes "the lighting of a new lantern" to the entity-attached surface-preposition oblique on the noun's own symbol (`(Of sk_refinement_1 sk_survey_1)`), and "Inflection only — never derivation" (decided by the word's function here, which is a noun) keeps the deverbal `lighting` as its own lemma rather than the verb class `light`.

The generality half stands — the sentence is a characterizing claim about a customary practice and the parse records it as one witnessed lighting, predicating ritual-hood and smallness of that witness rather than of the occurrence type — but the cited prohibition is overstated, since "never mint a witness for the gerund itself" governs a gerund subject whose MAIN PREDICATE is verbal and routed into a per-occurrence Skolem consequent, and the reviewer's own q2 gap concedes the copular case has no licensed form.

gaps_confirmed: A generic copular predication whose subject is a nominalized event ("The first lighting of X is a small ritual"): the gerund/nominalized-subject rule routes only a VERBAL main predicate into a per-occurrence Skolem consequent, and gives no form for a kind or property ascribed to the occurrence itself.

An ordinal restriction on a nominalized-event subject ("the FIRST lighting") has no stated carrier in the generic/rule route — Ordinal is defined over entities ranked on a scale, not over a rule's occurrence variable.
new_gaps: A deverbal event noun (lighting, refinement, destruction) has no licensed link to its underlying verb: the noun keeps its own form as its class and nothing licenses an `(Inheritance lighting light)`-style tie, so the same eventuality stated nominally and stated verbally yields two records with no symbol in common.
adjudication.defect_summary: The ordinal belongs on the lighting, not the lantern — `(Ordinal <lighting-symbol> 1 light)`. The subject is the nominalization itself — `(Member sk_lighting_1 lighting)` with its object argument as the entity-attached oblique `(Of sk_lighting_1 sk_lantern_1)` — not a reified `light` event carrying a `Patient`. For the standing half of the third issue NO compliant form is licensed: a kind-level property ascribed to a nominalized occurrence fits neither the copular kind route (the subject is an occurrence, not a kind) nor the gerund-subject rule route (whose consequent must be verbal), which is why it is filed as a gap.
adjudication.notes: Splitting "small ritual" into two atoms rather than fusing is right (a size adjective is incidental description), and no unlicensed head appears. The defects are slot, lemma and generality-level choices, not vocabulary.

fields.sentence: Each Council member touches the vessel of mire-essence before the first lighting.

q1_issues.issue: (Possession sk_vessel_1 mire_essence) encodes a container-and-contents of-phrase ('the vessel OF mire-essence'), which the genitive rule explicitly excludes from Possession alongside the measure case 'a cup of water', so the atom asserts a possessor link the text does not state.

q2_gaps: container/contents of-phrase on a concrete noun ('the vessel of mire-essence') - the possessive-NP section bars Possession for measure/container of-phrases but licenses no replacement head, and the entity-attached (Of ...) oblique is licensed only for a nominalization's object
review.notes: Everything else follows the instruction set: 'each <collective> member' as a per-member (PartOf $x sk_council_1) rule at STV 1.0 0.9 with its QuantifierPhrase companion naming the group kind, no group event beside it, the mire_essence genus with the noun modifier unexposed, Ordinal for 'the first lighting', and the temporal-anchor event-noun carrying only its class atom plus Before inside the consequent.

issues.reason: The genitive rule explicitly excludes a measure / container of-phrase ("a cup of water") from Possession, and since Possession is possessed-first the emitted atom additionally says the mire-essence owns the vessel - a possessor link the text does not state.

gaps_confirmed: container/contents (or material) of-phrase on a concrete noun ("the vessel of mire-essence") - Possession is barred by the measure/container exclusion and the entity-attached (Of ...) oblique is licensed only for a nominalization's object, so no head is licensed
adjudication.defect_summary: No compliant form is licensed for "the vessel of mire-essence" - Possession is barred by the measure/container exclusion, PartOf would be false (contents are not a component of their container), and the entity-attached (Of ...) oblique is licensed only for a nominalization's object - so the compliant parse types the vessel, fills its Theme slot, and leaves the of-phrase unencoded as a recorded gap, on the "D-Ashford has no licensed head" precedent.
adjudication.notes: Everything else follows the instruction set: "each Council member" as the per-member (PartOf $x sk_council_1) rule at 1.0 / 0.9 with a group-kind QuantifierPhrase and no group event beside it, no Name atom for the capitalized bare-class label "Council", mire_essence's noun modifier unexposed with the essence genus emitted, and the temporal-anchor event-noun carrying only its class atom, its Ordinal restrictor and the Before link inside the consequent.

fields.sentence: A replacement lantern needs no Council touch.
parse: (: lantern_no_need (And (Member sk_need_1 need) (Agent sk_need_1 sk_lantern_1) (Member sk_lantern_1 replacement_lantern) (Theme sk_need_1 council_touch)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

q2_gaps: negative determiner 'no' scoping over an OBJECT NP ('needs no Council touch'): the strength-0 event bundle carries the negation, but QuantifierPhrase is defined only over a subject/kind range (subject+predicate, or kind+verb-lemma), so the companion the instruction set calls mandatory for every explicit quantifier word has no slot shape here, and the 'no' vs plain 'not' distinction the copular-negation section preserves is lost
review.notes: The indefinite-singular subject correctly stays a witness typed inside the strength-0 bundle (verbal predicate, so not a generic), and the two compound genus atoms sit at top level as definitional decomposition. Capitalized 'Council' as a bare kind word is a common noun by default, so fusing council_touch with genus 'touch' and no exposed noun-modifier genus is the licensed route.
